title: Taiwan Says US Policy Is Unchanged After Chinese Report on Trump
summaryZh: 新華社稱川普不支持台獨，外交部：美方重申對台政策不變。
summaryHi: चीनी मीडिया के दावे के बाद ताइवान ने कहा कि अमेरिका की ताइवान नीति नहीं बदली।
summaryEs: Taiwán afirma que EE. UU. le confirmó que su política no ha cambiado pese a un informe chino.
summaryJa: 「トランプ氏は台湾独立を支持せず」との新華社報道に、外交部は米国の対台湾政策は不変と説明。
summaryKo: 신화통신의 트럼프 발언 보도에 대만 외교부는 미국의 대만 정책이 변함없다고 밝혔다.
summaryEn: Taiwan says the US has confirmed its Taiwan policy is unchanged, despite a Chinese report about Trump.
paragraphs: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) in Taiwan said on Tuesday that Washington had recently reaffirmed that its Taiwan policy remains unchanged, days after Chinese state media claimed that US President Donald Trump had told Xi Jinping he does not support Taiwan independence.

The claim appeared in a Xinhua report on November 19 about the meeting of the two leaders in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit. According to Xinhua, Xi urged Trump to handle Taiwan-related issues appropriately in order to avoid major setbacks in relations between the two powers.

The White House has neither confirmed nor denied the account. Its official readout of the talks did not mention Taiwan, and it issued only a general summary of the Asia trip by Trump, as it had done after the two previous meetings of the leaders.

Speaking to reporters, Hans Chiao, deputy director-general of the Department of North American Affairs at MOFA, said the US had restated its position to Taipei, though he declined to say whether Trump had made the remark. He dismissed Chinese state media as propaganda outlets and stressed that Taiwan is a sovereign, democratic country. Chiao added that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and other senior officials had repeatedly reaffirmed the policy.

According to the American Institute in Taiwan, US policy is guided by the Taiwan Relations Act, three joint communiqués with China and the Six Assurances. Washington opposes unilateral changes to the status quo and expects cross-strait differences to be resolved peacefully.
The foreign ministry of Taiwan says the policy of America on Taiwan has not changed. America told Taiwan this again recently.

Last week, US President Donald Trump met the leader of China, Xi Jinping, in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. After the meeting, a Chinese news agency wrote a story. It said Trump told Xi that America does not support Taiwan independence.
The White House did not say yes or no to this story. It did not talk about Taiwan in its own report on the meeting.

On Tuesday, a Taiwanese official, Hans Chiao, spoke to reporters. He said America told Taiwan that its policy is the same. He did not say if Trump said those words. He said Chinese news is often propaganda for the Chinese government.
America has a law about Taiwan called the Taiwan Relations Act. America says it wants peace between Taiwan and China. It does not want either side to change the situation alone.
sentZh: 台灣的外交部說，美國的對台政策沒有改變。
美國最近再次這樣告訴台灣。
上週，美國總統川普在中國城市深圳和中國領導人習近平見面。
會面後，一家中國通訊社寫了一篇報導。
報導說，川普告訴習近平美國不支持台灣獨立。
白宮對這篇報導沒有說是，也沒有說不是。
它在自己的會面報告中沒有提到台灣。
星期二，台灣官員焦國祐對記者發言。
他說美國告訴台灣，它的政策還是一樣。
他沒有說川普是否說過那些話。
他說中國的新聞常常是替中國政府做的宣傳。
美國有一部關於台灣的法律，叫做《台灣關係法》。
美國說它希望台灣和中國之間保持和平。
它不希望任何一方單獨改變現狀。

paragraphs: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Taiwan said on Tuesday that the United States had recently confirmed that its policy on Taiwan has not changed. The comment came after Chinese state media reported a surprising remark by US President Donald Trump.

On November 19, the Chinese news agency Xinhua reported on a meeting between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, held during the APEC summit. According to the report, Xi told Trump to handle the Taiwan issue carefully, and Trump said the US does not support Taiwan independence.
The White House has not confirmed or denied this. Its own summary of the talks did not mention Taiwan at all, which was also true after the previous meetings between the two leaders.

Hans Chiao, a senior official in the North American affairs department of the ministry, told reporters that Washington had repeated its position to Taipei. However, he did not say whether Trump had actually made the remark. He described Chinese state media as propaganda tools for Beijing and said Secretary of State Marco Rubio had confirmed the policy many times.

US policy is based on laws and agreements such as the Taiwan Relations Act and the Six Assurances. The US says it opposes any change to the current situation by either side and wants differences to be solved peacefully.
sentZh: 台灣外交部星期二表示，美國最近確認其對台政策沒有改變。
這番說法是在中國官方媒體報導美國總統川普一句令人意外的話之後提出的。
11月19日，中國新華社報導了川普與中國領導人習近平在亞太經合會峰會期間於深圳舉行的會面。
根據報導，習近平要川普謹慎處理台灣問題，而川普說美國不支持台灣獨立。
白宮沒有證實也沒有否認這件事。
它自己的會談摘要完全沒有提到台灣，兩位領導人之前的幾次會面後也是如此。
外交部北美事務部門的高階官員焦國祐告訴記者，華府已向台北重申其立場。
不過，他沒有說川普是否真的說過那句話。
他形容中國官方媒體是北京的宣傳工具，並說國務卿盧比歐已多次確認這項政策。
美國的政策是以《台灣關係法》和「六項保證」等法律與協議為基礎。
美國表示，它反對任何一方改變現狀，並希望以和平方式解決分歧。

paragraphs: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) in Taiwan said on Tuesday that Washington had recently reaffirmed that its Taiwan policy remains unchanged, days after Chinese state media claimed that US President Donald Trump had told Xi Jinping he does not support Taiwan independence.

The claim appeared in a Xinhua report on November 19 about the meeting of the two leaders in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit. According to Xinhua, Xi urged Trump to handle Taiwan-related issues appropriately in order to avoid major setbacks in relations between the two powers.

The White House has neither confirmed nor denied the account. Its official readout of the talks did not mention Taiwan, and it issued only a general summary of the Asia trip by Trump, as it had done after the two previous meetings of the leaders.

Speaking to reporters, Hans Chiao, deputy director-general of the Department of North American Affairs at MOFA, said the US had restated its position to Taipei, though he declined to say whether Trump had made the remark. He dismissed Chinese state media as propaganda outlets and stressed that Taiwan is a sovereign, democratic country. Chiao added that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and other senior officials had repeatedly reaffirmed the policy.

According to the American Institute in Taiwan, US policy is guided by the Taiwan Relations Act, three joint communiqués with China and the Six Assurances. Washington opposes unilateral changes to the status quo and expects cross-strait differences to be resolved peacefully.
sentZh: 台灣外交部星期二表示，華府最近重申其對台政策維持不變；就在幾天前，中國官方媒體聲稱美國總統川普曾告訴習近平，他不支持台灣獨立。
這個說法出現在新華社11月19日的報導中，內容是關於兩位領導人在亞太經合會峰會場邊於深圳的會面。
據新華社報導，習近平敦促川普妥善處理涉台問題，以避免兩大強權關係出現重大倒退。
白宮對這個說法既未證實也未否認。
它對會談的官方紀要沒有提到台灣，只發布了一份川普亞洲行的概括摘要，就像兩位領導人前兩次會面後的做法一樣。
外交部北美司副司長焦國祐對記者表示，美國已向台北重申其立場，但他不願透露川普是否說過那句話。
他駁斥中國官方媒體是宣傳機器，並強調台灣是一個主權獨立的民主國家。
焦國祐補充說，國務卿盧比歐和其他高層官員已多次重申這項政策。
根據美國在台協會的說法，美國政策以《台灣關係法》、與中國的三份聯合公報以及「六項保證」為指導。
華府反對單方面改變現狀，並期望兩岸分歧以和平方式解決。

paragraphs: The foreign ministry of Taiwan sought on Tuesday to dispel uncertainty over the stance of Washington, stating that the United States had recently reaffirmed that its Taiwan policy is unchanged. The assurance followed a Chinese state media report attributing to President Donald Trump the statement that America does not support Taiwan independence.

The report, published by Xinhua on November 19, described a meeting between Trump and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen held on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Xi reportedly urged his counterpart to handle Taiwan-related matters prudently so as to avoid serious setbacks in bilateral ties.

Conspicuously, the White House has neither confirmed nor refuted the account. Its readout omitted any reference to Taiwan, and no dedicated fact sheet was released, a pattern consistent with the two previous encounters between the leaders.

Hans Chiao, deputy director-general of the Department of North American Affairs at the ministry, told reporters that Washington had restated its position, while pointedly declining to say whether Trump had actually uttered the remark. Characterising Chinese state outlets as instruments of propaganda for Beijing, he insisted that Taiwan is a sovereign, independent democracy, and noted that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had reaffirmed the policy on multiple occasions.

Under its long-standing framework, built on the Taiwan Relations Act, three joint communiqués and the Six Assurances, the US opposes unilateral alterations to the status quo and expects cross-strait disputes to be settled peacefully.
sentZh: 台灣外交部星期二設法消除外界對華府立場的疑慮，表示美國最近重申其對台政策不變。
這項保證是在中國官方媒體一篇報導之後提出的，該報導指稱川普總統說過美國不支持台灣獨立。
新華社11月19日發布的這篇報導，描述了川普與習近平在亞太經合會峰會場邊於深圳舉行的會面。
據報導，習近平敦促對方審慎處理涉台事務，以免雙邊關係嚴重倒退。
引人注意的是，白宮對這個說法既未證實也未駁斥。
它的會談紀要完全沒有提及台灣，也沒有發布專門的情況說明，與兩位領導人前兩次會面的模式一致。
外交部北美司副司長焦國祐告訴記者，華府已重申其立場，但他刻意不說川普是否真的說過那句話。
他將中國官方媒體形容為北京的宣傳工具，堅稱台灣是一個主權獨立的民主國家，並指出國務卿盧比歐已多次重申這項政策。
在以《台灣關係法》、三份聯合公報和「六項保證」為基礎的長期架構下，美國反對單方面改變現狀，並期望兩岸爭端能和平解決。

paragraphs: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Taiwan has moved to reassure the public that American policy towards the island remains intact, despite a Chinese state media report suggesting that President Donald Trump had distanced himself from Taiwan independence.

According to Xinhua, which published its account on November 19, Trump made the remark during talks with Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Xi was also said to have warned that Taiwan should be handled appropriately to prevent significant setbacks in relations between Beijing and Washington.

Notably, the White House has neither verified nor denied this version of events. Its official summary of the meeting made no reference to Taiwan, an omission that mirrors its approach following the earlier summits of the two leaders.

Addressing reporters on Tuesday, Hans Chiao, a senior official responsible for North American affairs, confirmed that Washington had recently reiterated its unchanged position to Taipei. However, he refrained from commenting on whether Trump had genuinely made the statement, instead dismissing Chinese state media as propaganda outlets. He emphasised that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and other senior figures had repeatedly endorsed the existing policy.

That policy rests on the Taiwan Relations Act, three joint communiqués and the Six Assurances. Crucially, it opposes unilateral changes to the status quo by either side and insists that disputes across the Taiwan Strait be resolved by peaceful means.
sentZh: 台灣外交部已出面向民眾保證，美國對台政策依然不變，儘管一篇中國官方媒體報導暗示川普總統已與台灣獨立劃清界線。
根據新華社11月19日發布的報導，川普是在亞太經合會峰會場邊於深圳與習近平會談時說出這番話。
據稱習近平也警告，應妥善處理台灣問題，以防北京與華府的關係出現重大倒退。
值得注意的是，白宮對這個版本的說法既未證實也未否認。
它對這次會面的官方摘要完全沒有提及台灣，這種省略與兩位領導人先前幾次峰會後的處理方式如出一轍。
負責北美事務的高階官員焦國祐星期二對記者證實，華府最近已向台北重申其不變的立場。
不過，他避免評論川普是否真的說過那番話，而是駁斥中國官方媒體只是宣傳機器。
他強調，國務卿盧比歐和其他高層人士已多次表態支持現行政策。
這項政策建立在《台灣關係法》、三份聯合公報和「六項保證」之上。
關鍵在於，它反對任何一方單方面改變現狀，並堅持台灣海峽兩岸的爭端必須以和平方式解決。

noteEs.exampleTr: La subida de precios refleja una tendencia mundial.

noteJa.meaning: 反映する；よく似ている。
noteJa.usage: A mirrors B ＝A は B とよく似ている。
noteJa.exampleTr: 物価上昇は世界的な傾向を反映している。

noteKo.usage: A mirrors B = A가 B와 비슷하다.

noteEn.meaning: is very similar to something else.

moved.en: took action to do something (moved to)

neither.en: not one and not the other

north.ex: We drove north for three hours.

not.ex: I do not like cold tea.

notably.en: clearly; in a way people notice
notably.ex: The weather was notably warmer this week.

noted.ex: She noted that prices were falling.
noted.zh: 注意到；指出（it should be noted：值得注意的是）

november.en: the eleventh month of the year

occasions.ex: He was late on several occasions.

official.en: approved by the government or an authority
official.ex: The official report came out today.

officials.ex: Officials met to discuss the plan.

omission.ex: The omission of her name from the list upset her.

note.usage: 動詞 omit；常見 a notable/glaring omission。

example.en: The omission of his name from the list upset him.
example.zh: 名單上漏掉他的名字讓他很不高興。

noteHi.exampleTr: सूची से उसका नाम छूटने से वह नाराज़ हुआ।

noteEs.exampleTr: La omisión de su nombre en la lista le molestó.

noteJa.usage: 動詞は omit。notable omission など。
noteJa.exampleTr: リストから名前が漏れていたことに彼は腹を立てた。

noteKo.exampleTr: 명단에서 그의 이름이 빠진 것에 그는 화가 났다.

noteEn.meaning: something left out, or the act of leaving it out.

omitted.ex: His name was omitted from the report.

on.ex: Voting will go on for nine days.

opposes.ex: She opposes the new tax on fuel.

order.en: in order to: so that you can
order.ex: Arrive early in order to get a seat.

peace.ex: The soldiers help to keep the peace.
peace.zh: 和平（keep the peace：維持和平）

pointedly.ja: あからさまに；意図的に
pointedly.en: in a clear and deliberate way
pointedly.ex: He pointedly ignored the reporter's question.

policy.ex: The new policy helps first-time buyers.

position.ex: The party set out its position on tax.

powers.ex: The two powers signed a deal.

president.en: the elected head of a country

prevent.ex: Rules prevent managers from hiring staff.

previous.ex: The previous owner lived here for years.

propaganda.en: information used to make people support a political view
propaganda.ex: The leaflets were full of propaganda.

public.ex: The library is a public building.

published.ex: The report was published on Monday.

quo.ex: Many voters prefer the status quo.

readout.en: an official summary of a meeting
readout.ex: The readout did not mention trade.

reaffirmed.en: stated again that something is true
reaffirmed.ex: The president reaffirmed his support for the deal.

reassure.ex: The bank tried to reassure its customers.

example.en: The airline tried to reassure passengers that flights were safe.
example.zh: 航空公司試圖向乘客保證航班安全。

noteHi.exampleTr: एयरलाइन ने यात्रियों को उड़ानों के सुरक्षित होने का भरोसा दिलाया।

noteEs.exampleTr: La aerolínea intentó asegurar a los pasajeros que los vuelos eran seguros.

noteJa.exampleTr: 航空会社は乗客に運航は安全だと安心させようとした。

noteKo.exampleTr: 항공사는 승객들에게 운항이 안전하다고 안심시키려 했다.

noteEn.meaning: to make someone feel less worried.

reference.ex: The speech made no reference to taxes.

refrained.ex: He refrained from criticising his team.

example.en: Please refrain from using your phone during the show.
example.zh: 演出期間請勿使用手機。

noteHi.exampleTr: कृपया शो के दौरान फ़ोन का उपयोग न करें।

noteEs.exampleTr: Por favor, absténgase de usar el móvil durante el espectáculo.

noteJa.exampleTr: 公演中は携帯電話の使用をお控えください。

noteKo.exampleTr: 공연 중에는 휴대전화 사용을 삼가 주세요.

refuted.en: said that something is not true

reiterated.ex: She reiterated her support for the plan.

note.usage: 正式用語，常見於外交、政策：reiterate a position/commitment。

example.en: The minister reiterated that taxes would not rise.

noteHi.exampleTr: मंत्री ने दोहराया कि कर नहीं बढ़ेंगे।

noteEs.exampleTr: El ministro reiteró que no subirían los impuestos.

noteJa.meaning: 繰り返し述べた；改めて表明した。
noteJa.usage: 外交・政策の文脈で reiterate a position など。
noteJa.exampleTr: 大臣は増税しないと改めて表明した。

noteKo.usage: 외교·정책 문맥: reiterate a position 등.
noteKo.exampleTr: 장관은 세금을 올리지 않겠다고 재차 밝혔다.

noteEn.meaning: said something again, especially for emphasis.

relations.en: the way groups deal with each other
relations.ex: Relations between the two teams are good.

remains.ex: The shop remains open until late.

repeated.ex: He made repeated calls for help.

report.en: a news story about an event

reported.ex: The company reported higher sales this year.

reportedly.en: according to what people say or report
reportedly.ex: The deal is reportedly worth millions.
reportedly.ja: 伝えられるところでは

resolved.ex: The dispute was resolved after talks.

responsible.en: having a duty to deal with
responsible.ex: Who is responsible for road safety?

restated.ex: She restated her position at the meeting.

rests.ex: The plan rests on three ideas.

rubio.en: Rubio, a family name (Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State)

said.ex: She said the shop was closed.

say.ex: He would not say what happened.

says.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

secretary.en: a senior government minister (Secretary of State)
secretary.ex: The secretary of state visited Japan.

senior.ex: A senior manager answered our letter.

settled.en: ended an argument with an agreement

sheet.en: a piece of paper (fact sheet: a short paper of key facts)
sheet.ex: The office gave us a fact sheet.

shenzhen.en: a large city in southern China

side.en: one of two groups in a disagreement

sidelines.en: (on the sidelines) at the edge of a main event
sidelines.ex: They met on the sidelines of the summit.

significant.en: large or important enough to notice
significant.ex: There was a significant rise in prices.

situation.en: the conditions at a particular time

so.ex: It was raining, so we stayed home.

solved.en: found an answer to a problem

sought.ex: The ministry sought to calm fears.

sovereign.ex: The country set up a sovereign wealth fund.
sovereign.zh: 主權的；國家的（sovereign savings：國家儲蓄）

speaking.ex: Speaking up early can stop a conflict.

spoke.ex: The minister spoke about the plan.

stance.en: an opinion or position on something
stance.ex: The party changed its stance on taxes.

statement.ex: The club released a statement this morning.

states.en: parts of a country (United States: America)

stating.ex: He wrote a note stating that he was sorry.

status.ex: They want to keep the status quo.

story.ex: She read a story to the children.

strait.en: a narrow stretch of sea between two areas of land
strait.ex: Ships pass through the strait every day.

stressed.en: said strongly that it is important
stressed.ex: She stressed the need for care.

suggesting.ex: Her smile suggested she liked the gift.

summary.en: a short report of the main points
summary.ex: Read the summary before the meeting.

summit.ex: The climate summit lasted three days.

summits.ex: The two summits will be held in Dublin.

support.en: to agree with and help; to keep going

surprising.ex: The result was surprising to everyone.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

talk.ex: Talk to your manager about it.

talks.en: formal discussions to reach an agreement
talks.ex: Peace talks will start next month.

ties.ex: The two cities have strong cultural ties.

told.ex: My friend told me about the new café.

tools.en: things used to do a job
tools.ex: Put the kitchen tools in the drawer.

true.ex: Is it true that the shop is closing?

trump.en: Trump, a family name (Donald Trump, US president)

tuesday.ex: The meeting is on Tuesday morning.

uncertainty.en: a feeling of not knowing what will happen
uncertainty.ex: There is uncertainty about the future.

unchanged.ex: The price has stayed unchanged for years.

under.en: under the arrangement: by the deal; under way: happening
under.ex: Under the deal, each side pays half.

unilateral.en: done by one side without agreement

example.en: The company made a unilateral decision to cut wages.

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनी ने एकतरफ़ा वेतन कटौती का फ़ैसला किया।

noteEs.exampleTr: La empresa decidió unilateralmente recortar salarios.

noteJa.exampleTr: 会社は一方的に賃金カットを決めた。

noteEn.meaning: done by one side without the agreement of others.

urged.en: strongly asked someone to do something
urged.ex: She urged him to see a doctor.

uttered.ex: He never uttered a word about it.

version.en: one form of something that has many forms
version.ex: The new version of the game is faster.

want.en: to wish to have or do

wants.ex: She wants a quiet place to study.

warned.ex: Experts warned of a hot summer.

washington.en: the capital city of the United States

week.ex: I swim three times a week.

whether.en: used to express a choice (if or not)

words.en: in other words: saying it another way
words.ex: In other words, the plan has not changed.

wrote.en: put words on paper or screen
wrote.ex: He wrote a letter to the council.

xi.en: Xi, a family name (Xi Jinping, China's leader)
